title: Bid, ask, and the spread

inOneLine.simple: You buy at the higher price and sell at the lower one. The gap between them is a cost on every trade.

explain.simple: Every quote shows two prices. The [[bid]] is the price you can sell at. The [[ask]] is the price you can buy at, and it is slightly higher. The gap is the [[spread]]. If you buy and then sell straight away, you lose the spread. So every trade starts a little behind.
explain.balanced: A buy order fills at the ask and is closed by selling at the bid. A sell order fills at the bid and is closed by buying at the ask. The spread is therefore paid on every round trip. It changes with [[liquidity]] and often widens around major news and when the market is quiet.

assumptions: Account in USD; 1 pip on EUR/USD = 0.0001
steps: Cost of the spread on this trade = 1.5 × 1 USD = 1.50 USD, paid even if price never moves.
Spread cost = 3 × 10 = 30 USD for one round trip.

explainSimpler: Buying costs a little more than selling. That little difference is a fee you pay on every trade.
commonMistake: Placing a stop loss or target without allowing for the spread. A sell trade's stop is hit by the ask price, which can trigger it even when the chart's bid line never touched your level.

quickCheck.prompt: You want to buy EUR/USD at market. Which price do you get?

options.explanation: Right: buys fill at the ask, the higher price.
No: the bid is the price you can sell at.

options.text: The mid price, halfway between bid and ask
options.explanation: No: market orders do not fill at the mid. Buys fill at the ask.

quickCheck.prompt: Bid 1.2000, ask 1.2003. What is the spread in pips?

doItNow.instructions: In MetaTrader on your demo account, tap EUR/USD in the quotes list. Read the bid and the ask, work out the spread in pips, and write it down.

homework: Check the EUR/USD spread in MetaTrader around the London open and again late in the evening, and note both.
